summary.name: Making a Lion Bulletproof: SRE in Banking
summary.one_liner: A conference talk transcript by two ING engineers on how ING's Dutch retail bank built and runs its site reliability engineering (SRE) team, covering people, process and technology.
use_cases: Setting up an SRE team in a large organization
Deciding how SRE teams relate to product engineering
Hiring SREs with non-technical skills and mindset
Building a Prometheus-based monitoring and alerting stack
Structuring incident response and postmortem learning
Understanding the Google SRE reliability hierarchy in practice
summary.what_it_does: The talk describes ING's Dutch retail bank SRE team, which has seven engineers and works as a tool-building and consulting group rather than owning on-call for product teams. Its work centres on a white box monitoring and alerting stack called the Reliability Toolkit, which is based on Prometheus, plus a secure container platform and a public cloud service mesh. The speakers explain their hiring criteria, which favour learning ability, comfort with failure and willingness to teach over strict coding tests. They also outline their start as a six-month pilot after on-call engineers burned out, and how they run education, onboarding sessions, guilds and monthly demos to spread reliability practices. The transcript is a talk recording and does not present a product with pricing or a download.
notable: Describes ING's SRE team as a tool-building and consulting model where product teams keep service ownership
Reliability Toolkit: a white box monitoring and alerting stack built on Prometheus
Hiring focuses on non-technical traits such as learning ability, comfort with failure and insensitivity to hierarchy, with no standard code test
Started as a six-month SRE pilot led by engineers who had been on-call
caveats: Transcript of a talk, not a product page; no pricing or availability information is given
Describes one bank's internal setup, which may not transfer directly to other organizations
